stages.note: New AWS accounts often have 0 vCPU for GPU instances. Path A (recommended): Multicloud files the request for you, after your yes. Path B: you file it with your own AWS sign-in to the account. Do not create the pool before the quota is 4 or more. While you wait, continue with “Prepare your cluster”.

steps.h: Optional: ask your AI for GPU quota
steps.d: Say: “Request AWS quota for one on-demand L4 or A10G GPU in us-east-1 for my connected account.” Your AI shows the plan and files each request only after your yes. For a production workload it can plan, file and track every quota the workload needs, in each region.

steps.h: Path A: read the quota through Multicloud
steps.d: Shows the current limit, any open request and any recent denial for each GPU quota. It files nothing. L-DB2E81BA (on-demand G and VT instances) must be 8 or more: 8 or more, skip the request.

steps.h: Path A: Multicloud files 8 vCPU of GPU quota
steps.d: 8 vCPU covers one g6.2xlarge (L4) or g5.2xlarge (A10G). 4 vCPU is the minimum. The first line is needed only if you answered no to quota requests when you connected the account (organization owner only).
steps.c:
mctl cloud-account allow-quota-requests <cloud-account-id>   # only if not allowed yet
mctl cloud-account quota-request <cloud-account-id> --region us-east-1 \
  --code L-DB2E81BA --desired 8

steps.h: Path B: read your current GPU quota
steps.d: Only with your own AWS sign-in to the account. The command prints one number: your vCPU limit for on-demand G and VT instances. 8 or more: skip the request. Less than 8: request 8 (one g6.2xlarge or g5.2xlarge needs 8; 4 fits only the smallest L4 or A10G size).
steps.c:
aws service-quotas get-service-quota --service-code ec2 --quota-code L-DB2E81BA \
  --region us-east-1 --query Quota.Value --output text

steps.h: Path B: request 8 vCPU of GPU quota
steps.d: 8 vCPU covers one g6.2xlarge (L4) or g5.2xlarge (A10G). 4 vCPU is the minimum.
steps.c:
aws service-quotas request-service-quota-increase --service-code ec2 \
  --quota-code L-DB2E81BA --desired-value 8 --region us-east-1

steps.d: AWS can open a support case and ask for your use case. Reply: “Evaluation of LLM inference on one L4 or A10G GPU, on-demand, for about one week.”

This takes hours to a few days. Your AI can check every 2 hours and tell you when AWS answers. Meanwhile continue with “Prepare your cluster”, but do not create the GPU pool yet: it costs while it waits. Open request: wait. Limit 8 or more: done. Denied: tell your Multicloud contact.
steps.g: Path B, with your own AWS sign-in: aws service-quotas list-requested-service-quota-change-history-by-quota --service-code ec2 --quota-code L-DB2E81BA --region us-east-1 --query 'RequestedQuotas[].[Status,DesiredValue,Created]' --output table
